label: Write
summary: Turn speech into clean text for the field focused when you choose Stop, with a saved recovery path when delivery is blocked.
proof: Local transcription is the default; optional shaping is a separate decision.

opening.title: Speak once. Stop at the field where your words belong.
opening.summary: Use Mumble’s deliberate Dictate command and speak while the Island shows what is happening. Keep or return focus to the intended field before you choose Stop. When Stop is requested, Mumble freezes that field as the destination. It then attempts one delivery.

demonstration.spoken: Move the design review to Thursday and send the notes before lunch.
demonstration.note: Illustrative cursor close-up—not a live transcription. The Mumble workspace above is a genuine product capture.

states.label: Choose cursor
states.title: Keep the intended field ready for Stop.
states.body: Place the cursor in the writing field where you want the finished text. Keep it focused, or return to it, before choosing Stop.

states.label: Speak
states.title: Mumble makes its state visible.
states.body: Use the global Dictate command and speak. Before choosing Stop, keep or return focus to the intended field. The Island shows Listening, then Transcribing.

states.label: Text returned
states.title: Stop freezes the intended destination.
states.body: When Stop is requested, Mumble freezes the focused field for one target-bound insertion. If delivery cannot complete, the result remains recoverable in the Deck.
states.field: Project note — Move the design review to Thursday and send the notes before lunch.

mechanism.title: One deliberate command. One visible route back.
mechanism.summary: Write keeps the Stop-time destination, processing state, privacy route, delivery attempt, and recovery path in one understandable sequence.

steps.title: Keep the intended field focused for Stop
steps.body: Place the cursor in a writable field. Keep or return focus to the intended field before you choose Stop. Mumble then uses the field focused at Stop instead of asking you to move into a separate editor.
steps.proof: The destination is frozen when Stop is requested—not when recording starts.

steps.title: Start with the deliberate global Dictate command
steps.body: Invoke Dictate from the application you are already using. The Island shows Listening, then Transcribing, so recording and processing are visible rather than implied.
steps.proof: The same global command starts and stops the dictation.

steps.title: Transcribe on this computer by default
steps.body: Local transcription is the default. Recorded audio stays on this computer unless the user explicitly selects Cloud transcription.
steps.proof: Optional shaping is a separate finished-text decision.

steps.title: Return once, or recover safely
steps.body: Mumble attempts to insert the finished text at the field frozen when Stop was requested. If insertion cannot complete, the result is saved in the Deck and History for Copy or Paste latest instead of being sent again automatically.
steps.proof: Later focus changes do not authorize a new destination or a second blind insertion.

tasks.title: Everyday notes
tasks.summary: Add a complete thought to the note already open in front of you.
steps: Place the cursor at the point where the note should continue.
Use the global Dictate command and speak the thought in ordinary language.
Keep or return focus to that field before you choose Stop; the Island then shows the transition into transcription.
Continue from the inserted text, or use the saved Deck result if delivery could not complete.

tasks.title: Longer text
tasks.summary: Draft a connected passage without replacing the document you already chose.
steps: Place the cursor in the draft where the next passage belongs.
Start Dictate and speak the passage at a comfortable pace.
Keep or return focus to that field before you choose Stop; the Island then shows the transition into transcription.
Review the returned text in the draft, or recover the finished result from the Deck if insertion was blocked.

tasks.title: Across applications
tasks.summary: Carry the same Write sequence into another writable desktop application.
steps: Open the destination application and place its cursor in the intended field.
Invoke the global Dictate command without leaving that application.
Speak, then keep or return focus to the intended field before you choose Stop.
Mumble attempts one return to the field frozen at Stop; if that field is unavailable at delivery, it keeps the text in the Deck rather than inserting elsewhere.

label: Capture
summary: Record microphone meetings into a local, searchable working record you can review and export.
proof: Mumble saves the recording locally before transcription and later analysis.

label: Shape
summary: Give finished text a deliberate job, including Prompt, Email, Reply, and Deck actions.
proof: Cloud text shaping is optional and sends finished text—not recorded audio—through the chosen route.

label: Listen
summary: Turn supported documents into a library-first listening workspace with saved progress, find, bookmarks, and optional summaries.
proof: Playback uses the configured online text-to-speech route and requires network access, a user provider key, provider availability, and provider credits.

opening.title: Let the document keep your place while you listen.
opening.summary: Add supported documents to Reader, choose an online voice and speed, then play or pause while Mumble preserves the document, reading position, progress, find results, and bookmarks in one library-first flow.

demonstration.note: Genuine Mumble Reader interface with demonstration library content. The close-up states explain the accepted flow and do not play audio on this website.

states.label: Choose document
states.title: Start from the document, not a blank player.
states.body: Open a saved document from All, Collections, History, search, Starred, or Continue Reading. Reader keeps library and progress context visible before playback begins.
states.detail: Illustrative close-up based on supported Reader library states

states.label: Listen
states.title: Play or pause with voice and speed visible.
states.body: Reader speech uses the configured online text-to-speech route. Network access, a user provider key, provider availability, and available provider credits are required before audio can be created.
states.detail: Illustrative playback state; this static website produces no audio

states.label: Return
states.title: Resume from the saved reading position.
states.body: Return through Continue Reading, inspect progress, find a passage, and use bookmarks without losing the document position that Reader has retained.
states.field: Resume at 22% · Find and bookmarks available
states.detail: Illustrative continuity state using supported Reader controls

mechanism.title: The document stays primary. Online speech remains explicit.
mechanism.summary: Listen connects supported document import, a saved library, configured online playback, navigation, progress, and a separately chosen summary route without hiding their boundaries.

steps.title: Add a supported document
steps.body: Paste plain text, or open TXT, Markdown, PDF, DOCX, HTML, EPUB, RTF, CSV, XLSX, PPTX, or ODT. Reader extracts a structured document and adds it to the saved library.
steps.proof: Unsupported formats are not advertised as Reader inputs.

steps.title: Organise the saved library
steps.body: Use All, Collections, History, library search, Starred, and Continue Reading to return to the right document rather than rebuilding a temporary playlist.
steps.proof: Collections and reading history remain part of Reader's library-first model.

steps.title: Choose the online voice, then play or pause
steps.body: Select the configured provider and model, then choose the voice and speed. Reader sends short document passages through that frozen online text-to-speech route to create audio, then keeps play, pause, stop, and progress close to the document.
steps.proof: Network access, a user provider key, provider availability, and available provider credits are required.

steps.title: Find, bookmark, and move through the document
steps.body: Find text inside the open document, move between matches, add a bookmark at the current position, and choose another passage without separating navigation from playback.
steps.proof: Find and bookmarks operate on the document already open in Reader.

steps.title: Keep reading position and progress
steps.body: Reader records the current word as the saved reading position, reports progress, and offers Continue Reading so a later session can return to the retained place.
steps.proof: Closing Find or Summary restores useful focus without moving the saved reading or playback position.

steps.title: Choose an optional summary separately
steps.body: Summary is not part of playback. When you choose it and a configured analysis route is ready, Mumble sends document text to that provider; the resulting summary can then be read through the separately configured speech route.
steps.proof: A summary action and text-to-speech playback are two distinct online decisions.

tasks.title: Long document
tasks.summary: Add a supported long document and keep its reading controls close to the text.
steps: Open Reader and add a supported document or paste plain text; it joins the saved library before playback.
Choose the configured online text-to-speech provider, model, voice, and speed.
Confirm network access, a user provider key, provider availability, and available provider credits before choosing Play.
Play or pause while the document, current position, and progress remain visible together.

tasks.title: Resume reading
tasks.summary: Return later without searching manually for the last spoken passage.
steps: Open Reader and choose Continue Reading or the saved document from the library.
Review the retained reading position and progress before audio starts.
Check that the configured online speech route is ready, then keep or change voice and speed.
Choose Play to continue from the saved position, or select another passage deliberately.

tasks.title: Find a passage
tasks.summary: Move directly to matching text while keeping playback and position understandable.
steps: Open the saved document and choose Find in document.
Enter a phrase and move through the matching passages with Previous or Next.
Choose the intended passage; Reader updates the visible document position without creating a separate result.
Resume configured online playback there, or add a bookmark for a later return.

tasks.title: Retain progress
tasks.summary: Finish a session with a durable place to return, even when no summary is requested.
steps: Pause or stop Reader when the listening session should end.
Reader retains the document's current word position and updates its visible progress.
Return through the library, Collections, History, Starred, or Continue Reading when the document is needed again.
Choose Summary only as a separate optional document-text action; retained playback progress does not depend on it.

label: Find
summary: Use Mumble Find to search local apps and files without hosted results entering the list.
proof: Web Search is separate and sends selected text online only after provider-named confirmation.
